set.per_unit_cap: Units stay exempt if an existing tenant's income rises to 140% AMI in tax credit units or to 100% AMI in other agreement-restricted units (100% rule runs FY 2024-25 through 2028-29; reported on BOE-267-L3 and L4). Revenue and Taxation Code 214(g)(1)(C) caps the exemption at $20,000,000 of assessed value per taxpayer per fiscal year (single or multiple properties), and only where the exemption rests solely on the 90 percent lower income occupancy test for a property not owned by a limited partnership. Projects with tax-exempt bonds, government loans or grants (214(g)(1)(A)) or low-income housing tax credits (214(g)(1)(B)) are outside the cap; LP-owned projects with a nonprofit managing general partner must have tax credits or government financing to qualify (BOE Publication 149). Not a statewide cap.
set.next_deadline: File BOE-267 (first year) or BOE-267-A (annual) with the Assessor by February 15 each year (next: February 15, 2027) with BOE-267-L, L1, L2 and worksheets as applicable. Late claims: 90% of tax canceled if filed by January 1 of the next calendar year, 85% after (BOE Publication 149). The Yolo ACE website does not post exemption instructions; call the Assessor's office.
set.prevailing_wage_basis: Property tax exemption; no construction funds are provided, so the exemption itself does not make a project public works.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: the cited BOE county contacts page is only an assessor directory. Checked BOE Publication 149 and Rev. and Tax. Code 214 and 255. The $20 million cap is per taxpayer, not statewide, and applies only to non-LP claims under the 90% occupancy test.

reason: Material: per_unit_cap called the $20 million cap a statewide assessed-value cap, but Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)(1)(C) applies it per taxpayer only to non-LP claims qualifying solely on the 90 percent occupancy test.
